title: Your Code Has Bugs. Lean4 Has Proofs: Formal Verification for Engineers — Varun Pant, AWS
talk_summary: Varun Pant argues that LLM judges, tests, and human review cannot prove correctness for all inputs, and that formal verification (Lean4, Verus, SMT solvers) can, with humans owning the specification and machines owning code and proof. He shows examples: AI-converted zlib to Lean with 32k lines of proof, Cedar's Rust-vs-Lean differential random testing with 100M tests nightly, and AWS's Strata IR for multi-language verification.

takeaways.technique: Spec-first review gate (spec as upstream artifact)
takeaways.what_they_do: Write an explicit specification of what 'correct' means, validate the spec itself (human review or testing it on sample inputs), then have the agent implement against it and check the implementation matches the spec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: humans own the specification and machines own the code and proof

takeaways.technique: Differential random testing against a reference model
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a simple reference implementation/model and run large volumes of randomized differential tests comparing production code output to the model output; block releases on mismatch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: about 100 million differential random tests uh run nightly. No version ships until this is satisfied

takeaways.technique: Property-based / for-all-inputs checks instead of example tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Frame correctness as properties that must hold for every input, not just the tested examples, and let a checker (proof or property test) enforce them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Tests? They only check some inputs, not all.

takeaways.what_they_do: The AI decomposes a large proof into helper lemmas (subgoals), proves each independently, then assembles them into the final theorem, with a small kernel checking the assembly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI decomposed the problem into lemmas, which are subgoals. It proved each of them using tactics

takeaways.technique: Small trusted checker separate from the generator
takeaways.what_they_do: Separate the thing that produces work (tactics/AI) from a small, independently checkable verifier (kernel) that only validates the result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you only need to trust the small kernel
